headline: Materials Lead a Broad Rally, but the Week Ends in the Red
body_html:
Equities closed Friday's session on a constructive note, with advancers outnumbering decliners by more than two to one across the 550-name universe — 370 stocks finishing higher against 176 in the red. The tone was decidedly pro-cyclical: Materials led all sectors with a gain of 1.48%, Homebuilders added 1.14%, and Software rose 0.98%, a lineup that suggested investors were selectively reaching for risk heading into the weekend. Healthcare and Consumer followed in the middle of the pack, while Energy barely cleared the flat line at 0.19%.

The session's standout mover was Alpha Metallurgical Resources, the metallurgical coal producer, which surged 8.09% to pace all gainers. Albemarle, the lithium specialist, was close behind with a 6.75% advance, reinforcing the commodity-materials bid that defined the day's character. On the payments side, Remitly climbed 7.93%, while TG Therapeutics and Hims & Hers Health each added more than 6% to lift the healthcare complex. The lone blemish on an otherwise solid tape was Semiconductors, the only sector to close in negative territory, off 0.23%.

Despite Friday's gains, the week as a whole ended with losses — a reminder that single-session strength does not always resolve broader uncertainty. Bond yields and geopolitical tensions, particularly around Iran, kept a ceiling on sentiment all week, and those headwinds showed little sign of abating as markets closed for the weekend.

briefs.headline: Dalio Flags Debt Danger, Steers Toward Hard Assets
briefs.body: Bridgewater founder Ray Dalio warned that a recent Treasury Department personnel move is an early signal that a sovereign debt crisis may be drawing closer. Dalio advised investors to increase exposure to gold and bitcoin as hedges against what he views as a deteriorating fiscal trajectory in the United States.

briefs.headline: Strait of Hormuz Contingencies Discussed Among NATO Allies
briefs.body: NATO member states held talks this week about potential options for protecting shipping lanes through the Strait of Hormuz, though discussions explicitly excluded any formal alliance involvement. The conversations reflect deepening concern about supply-chain disruption as the Iran conflict drags into its sixth month and tanker-route risk remains elevated.

briefs.headline: Gold Finds Its Footing as Dollar Softens and Debt Fears Mount
briefs.body: Bullion rebounded Friday after a turbulent stretch, drawing fresh demand from investors rattled by rising bond yields, dollar weakness, and growing anxiety over government debt levels globally. The move dovetailed with Dalio's public comments, reinforcing a week-long narrative that hard assets are regaining favor as portfolio ballast.

briefs.headline: Citadel Unwinds Bulk of Situational Awareness Book
briefs.body: Ken Griffin disclosed that Citadel has unwound more than 80% of the risk positions held within its Situational Awareness portfolio, a notable de-risking move from one of Wall Street's most closely watched hedge funds. The disclosure adds to a broader picture of large institutions trimming exposures ahead of what many expect to be a volatile autumn.

briefs.headline: South African Rand Posts Strongest Read Since Iran Hostilities Began
briefs.body: The South African rand touched its firmest level against major currencies since the outbreak of the Iran conflict, a milestone that analysts attributed to recovering commodity prices and tentative signs of emerging-market stabilization. The currency's rebound tracked closely with Friday's strength in materials and metals-linked equities.

briefs.headline: Wall Street Wrestles With Round-the-Clock Futures Debate
briefs.body: A simmering debate over perpetual futures — essentially continuous, never-expiring securities that trade around the clock — gained urgency this week as market-structure professionals raised concerns about risk management, margin frameworks, and regulatory oversight. The discussion reflects broader tension between innovation-driven demand for always-on markets and the infrastructure required to support them safely.
